raw.note:
Data (synthetic, from MNIST train): an MNIST digit (28x28) slides left -> right across a 28x52 canvas,
3 px per frame, 8 frames (x offset = x0 + 3k, x0 random in 0..3).
  joint model : the same U-Net as the digit model but with 8 input/output channels = the 8 frames stacked,
                so every denoising step sees the whole clip at once.
  frame model : the same U-Net with 1 channel, trained on single frames drawn from the same clips.
Both: DDPM eps-loss, linear beta, T=1000, class-conditional (10% label dropout), same steps/batch/lr.
Sampling: DDIM 50 steps, w=1. Independent clip = 8 frames from the frame model with 8 independent noises.
Metrics: flicker = mean |frame_{k+1} - shift(frame_k, 3 px)| (pixels in [0,1]); horizontal centre of mass per frame,
fitted slope (px/frame, truth = 3) and the residual std of a straight-line fit.

video_toy_noise_correlation.note: Episode 22 toy: frame-to-frame consistency from correlated starting noise (uses the trained digit model). A "clip" = 8 frames. Every frame is a digit generated by the DDPM-trained U-Net (DDIM 50 steps, w = 1, label fixed per clip). Frame k starts from  eps_k = sqrt(rho) * eps_shared + sqrt(1 - rho) * eps_k_own   (unit variance for any rho; the "mixed noise" idea of PYoCo, Ge et al. 2023).  rho = 0: frames drawn independently; rho = 1: one shared noise. Motion is IMPOSED by pasting frame k 3 px further right on a 28x52 canvas; the model is not asked to make motion. What we measure is whether the digit stays the same digit from frame to frame (identity/style flicker):   flicker   = mean |frame_{k+1} - shift(frame_k, 3 px)| on the canvas, pixels in [0, 1] (0 = perfectly consistent)   change_px = mean L2 distance between consecutive 28x28 digits, pixels in [0, 1] (784 dims)
